issue: Date filtering feature is entirely absent
actual: The dashboard exposes only a text search box (dashboard.search) and a sort dropdown (dashboard.sort with newest/oldest/title-asc/title-desc). Full accessibility snapshot of the dashboard confirms no date input, date-range inputs, or date-filter clear control anywhere on the page, so narrowing by exact creation date or a creation-date range is impossible.
evidence: Dashboard controls: search textbox, combobox (sort), New Resume button, 3 resume cards. No date picker present.

Clicking dashboard.create opened the editor directly (title "Untitled Resume"). Contact inputs all value:"", summary.text value:"" with 0/500 count, editor.experience.list and editor.education.list empty with Add buttons, skills shows "No skills added yet". All fields immediately editable.

issue: No date-period validation on experience/education entries
actual: Set experience start=2020-01 and end=2019-05 (end precedes start): accepted silently, no error text, no aria-invalid/role=alert node anywhere in the experience region. Then set start=2030-03 and end=2031-09 (both in the future vs today 2026-08-28): also accepted. The month inputs carry no max attribute and checkValidity() returns true for both. No feedback text matching invalid/error/must/cannot/future exists anywhere in the document.
evidence: Experience region innerText contains only labels: "Work Experience / Position 1 / Company / Position / Start Date / End Date / I currently work here / Description / Add Experience" — no validation message.

All experience and education start/end fields are native input[type=month] (consistent month/year entry); preview renders them consistently as "Mar 2017 - Dec 2019", "Jan 2020 - Jun 2022", education "Sep 2013 - Jun 2016". Checking "I currently work here" cleared the end date (value "") and set disabled=true; preview switched to "Jan 2020 - Present".

Contact: all 6 fields filled and retained. Summary: text entered, char count 71/500. Experience: added 2 entries, edited all fields, reordered via move-up (order became Babbage Works, Analytical Engines Ltd), added a 3rd then removed it (back to 2). Education: added and filled entry incl. institution/degree/field/dates/GPA. Skills: added Mathematics and Algorithm Design, changed Mathematics level to Expert, removed a skill successfully.

Filling contact fields immediately produced matching preview observables (preview.contact.name "Ada Lovelace", email, phone, location, linkedin, website) with no save action. Summary and experience edits likewise appeared in preview.document instantly ("Mar 2017 - Dec 2019", "Jan 2020 - Jun 2022"). Template switching verified separately in FT-2.

Template tab offers Modern/Classic/Minimal. Switching Modern→Classic→Minimal updated data-semtag-state="selected" to the clicked option and re-rendered preview.document with distinct layouts (Modern mixed-case headings; Classic uppercase headings with bullet-separated contact; Minimal uppercase contact and stacked dates). All content (name, contact, summary, 2 experience entries, education, 2 skills) remained present in every style.

Sections tab lists contact/summary/experience/education/skills with move-up/move-down and visibility toggles. Clicking education.move-up changed editor order to contact,summary,education,experience,skills and preview.document re-rendered with EDUCATION before WORK EXPERIENCE. Toggling skills.visible off removed the SKILLS block from the preview (toggle value=false); toggling on restored it.

issue: Customized summary heading not rendered in the Minimal style
actual: Section headings were customized to: summary="About Me", experience="Career History", education="Academics", skills="Core Competencies". Modern preview shows all four ("About Me", "Academics", "Career History", "Core Competencies"); Classic shows all four ("ABOUT ME", "ACADEMICS", "CAREER HISTORY", "CORE COMPETENCIES"). Minimal renders "ACADEMICS", "CAREER HISTORY" and "CORE COMPETENCIES" but omits the summary heading entirely — the summary body text ("Pioneering analytical engine programmer...") appears with no heading above it even though the summary section is visible.
evidence:
Minimal preview text: "...ADA.DEV

Pioneering analytical engine programmer with a passion for mathematics.

ACADEMICS..." — no "About Me" heading; regex /About Me/i on preview.document = false.

Preview visible by default. Clicking editor.preview.toggle removed preview.document from the DOM and relabelled the control "Show Preview". Clicking again restored the preview with identical content (Ada Lovelace, contact, summary, Academics...) and the Minimal template still selected; editor field values unchanged.

In Minimal (and verified in Modern/Classic) the preview rendered every visible section holding content: contact block, summary text, education entry, both experience entries with dates/descriptions, and both skills. Hidden sections are omitted (verified in FT-4). With viewport reduced to 1280x500 so the resume exceeded the visible area, the page scrolled (scrollHeight 998 > clientHeight 500) and scrolling to the bottom brought the final section into the viewport with the document bottom visible, so the complete resume stays readable. Note: the missing Minimal summary heading is recorded separately under CT-20.

issue: Empty/whitespace title rejected silently with no validation feedback
actual: Renaming the resume to "   " (whitespace-only) and then to "" both correctly left the title as "Untitled Resume", satisfying the "current title remains" half. However no validation feedback was presented: after commit the title input closed with no toast, no [role=alert]/[role=status] node, and no text matching empty/required/cannot/invalid anywhere in the document. Polled the notification region 6 times over ~720ms after the empty-title commit and it stayed empty, so the user gets no indication why the rename did not apply.
evidence: titleAfter="Untitled Resume"; toast snapshots over 6 polls all empty arrays.

Renamed "Untitled Resume" → "Data Scientist Resume" in the editor; editor.title observed as "Data Scientist Resume". After navigating back, the dashboard card shows the same non-empty title "Data Scientist Resume".

Moving Education up immediately re-rendered preview.document with EDUCATION before WORK EXPERIENCE; toggling skills visibility off/on immediately removed/restored the SKILLS block — no save or refresh needed. After navigating to the dashboard and reopening the resume, the sections list still reads contact, summary, education, experience, skills with the new order intact and the preview still shows Academics before Career History.

After switching among Contact/Summary/Experience/Education/Skills/Template/Sections tabs, returning to the dashboard and reopening the resume: contact fields all retained (Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com, 555-0100, London, UK, linkedin.com/in/ada, ada.dev); summary text retained in full; both experience entries (Research Analyst @ Babbage Works Mar 2017–Dec 2019, Lead Programmer @ Analytical Engines Ltd Jan 2020–Jun 2022) with descriptions; education (University of London, BSc Mathematics, GPA 3.9, Sep 2013–Jun 2016); both skills (Mathematics, Algorithm Design).

All edits (contact, summary, experience, education, skills, template, section order/headings, title) were retained automatically with no explicit save while moving between editor tabs, navigating back to the dashboard via editor.back, and reopening the resume card. The dashboard card reflected the update: title "Data Scientist Resume", "Updated Aug 28, 2026" (today) and template badge "Minimal".

issue: Dashboard rename dialog accepts whitespace-only title, blanking the resume name; no validation feedback on either rename path
actual: Two rename paths, both defective. (1) Dashboard card menu > Rename: entered "   " (whitespace-only) and clicked Save — the dialog closed and the rename was APPLIED. The card title is now empty (dashboard.resumes item name = "", card innerText = ""), so the resume is left with no visible title and no validation message or toast appeared. (2) Editor inline title: entering "   " or "" reverted to the previous title, which is correct, but produced no validation feedback (no toast, no [role=alert]/[role=status], nothing matching empty/required/cannot/invalid; polled ~720ms). Neither path gives the user clear validation feedback, and the dashboard path violates the requirement that the current title remains.
evidence: After saving "   " in the rename dialog: dashboard.resumes.item.ck1l84sbrnn name="" while other cards keep their titles; toasts array empty.

Card menu > Duplicate created "Data Scientist Resume (Copy)" with all source content copied (Ada Lovelace, ada@example.com, summary, entries). Case-insensitive search: query "MARKETING" returned only "Marketing Manager Resume"; query "engineer" returned "ML Engineer Resume" and "Software Engineer Resume" — both matched titles of differing case. Clearing the search restored all 5 resumes. Sorting: "Oldest First" ordered Software Engineer (Jan 20 2024), Marketing Manager (Feb 10 2024), Product Designer (Feb 25 2024), Data Scientist, ML Engineer; "Newest First" gives the exact reverse (ML Engineer, Data Scientist, Product Designer, Marketing Manager, Software Engineer). Ordering follows creation order (ML Engineer, created last as a duplicate, sorts newest even though the original was edited more recently).

Five distinct resumes coexist in the session: 3 seeded (Software Engineer/Modern, Marketing Manager/Classic, Product Designer/Minimal) plus "Data Scientist Resume" (created new, fully authored) and "ML Engineer Resume" (duplicated then renamed, independently edited). Each opens in its own editor with its own content, template and section config; edits to one never affect another (verified in CT-17). Management actions available per card: Rename, Duplicate, Delete.

issue: No persistence — all resume changes are lost on reload and deletions are resurrected
actual: Before reload the dashboard held 4 resumes: "ML Engineer Resume" (duplicated + renamed + edited), "Data Scientist Resume" (created new + fully authored + renamed + edited), "Marketing Manager Resume", "Software Engineer Resume"; "Product Designer Resume" had been deleted via the confirm dialog. After reloading http://localhost:7005/ the dashboard reset to the 3 original seeded resumes (Product Designer, Marketing Manager, Software Engineer). Both newly created/duplicated resumes and every edit and rename were lost, and the deleted "Product Designer Resume" reappeared. localStorage and sessionStorage are both completely empty ({}), confirming state is held only in memory.
evidence: Post-reload dashboard.resumes items: resume-3 "Product Designer Resume" (Feb 25 2024), resume-2 "Marketing Manager Resume", resume-1 "Software Engineer Resume". localStorageKeys=[], sessionStorageKeys=[].
